title: Organizational Inertia
equation: Change Capacity = Burning Platform × Leadership Conviction × Structural Redesign ÷ Existing Inertia
hook: You've explained the new plan five times. The team nods. Nothing changes.
statement: Established teams resist change even when it's obviously needed. Redesigning the structure beats persuading people.
explainer: Speeches and memos rarely move a team. Changing incentives, who decides what, and how people are grouped does. When the setup rewards the old way, the old way wins.
sop: Treat resistance as a design problem, not a character flaw.
Make the reason for change concrete and urgent.
Change incentives so the new way actually pays off.
Score Burning Platform, Leadership Conviction, Structural Redesign, and Existing Inertia from 1 to 10.
equation_example: Burning Platform 7, Leadership Conviction 8, Structural Redesign 4, Existing Inertia 6. (7 × 8 × 4) ÷ 6 = 37.3. Higher means the change will stick. Lower, especially with weak Structural Redesign, means talking alone won't move it.
question: Name the one incentive or rule you'd change so your biggest needed shift happens on its own.
